claims.claim: Secret and certificate values are encrypted with AES-256-GCM envelope encryption and a KEK outside the database.

evidence.name: should encrypt and decrypt through the provider
serializes only status fields

claims.claim: Backups are age-encrypted, checksum-verified, and restore into a fresh database.

evidence.name: should create a verifiable encrypted archive and reject tampering
should restore into an empty target and verify secrets, audit, CA, and agent certificate

claims.claim: Agents authenticate with short-lived client certificates on a separate mTLS listener.

evidence.name: rejects missing and untrusted client certificates and accepts the trusted one
should join with a valid token and create one certificate and one consumer

claims.claim: Every unsafe browser request requires a same-origin check and a per-session CSRF token.

evidence.name: should reject an unsafe request with a wrong CSRF token
should add credentials and the CSRF header to unsafe methods

claims.claim: Browser sessions rotate with a short retry receipt; CLI refresh families rotate and detect reuse.

evidence.name: should rotate the secret and CSRF token on refresh while keeping the session identity
should revoke the whole family and reject the current refresh token when a rotated token is reused

claims.claim: The audit chain detects edits, deletions, and tail truncation when a surviving link or checkpoint exists.

evidence.name: should detect an edited details value and an edited hash
should detect a deleted tail even when a newer checkpoint exists

claims.claim: Secret values are not stored in browser storage, URLs, JavaScript-visible cookies, or logs.

evidence.name: should mask the value and read it only on reveal
masks the documented top-level, one-level, and request-body paths

claims.claim: Reference containers run non-root with read-only roots, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, and resource limits.

evidence.name: validateCompose

claims.claim: The runtime database role cannot run DDL or delete audit events, and migrations run as a separate owner role.

evidence.name: lets the runtime role read and write data but not run DDL or delete audit events

claims.claim: Certificate expiry warnings fire once at 30, 14, and 7 days.

evidence.name: should fire 30, 14, and 7-day warnings once per threshold

claims.claim: The web UI is keyboard operable and passes automated accessibility checks for the login, secret, and audit screens.

evidence.name: should pass axe on secret detail

claims.claim: A restore drill covers backup, restore into a fresh target, audit verification, and a pre-backup agent certificate.

evidence.name: should restore into an empty target and verify secrets, audit, CA, and agent certificate

claims.claim: Release images are amd64 and arm64, signed with Cosign keyless, have an SBOM and provenance, and are scanned for HIGH/CRITICAL findings.

evidence.name: should publish release images to Docker Hub

evidence.check: The v1.0.0 and v1.0.1 releases published signed amd64 and arm64 images to Docker Hub with SBOM and provenance attestations.

claims.claim: The OpenAI Codex Security scan is a manual, periodic check. It is not part of CI/CD and does not block a release.

evidence.check: Run codex-security manually when needed and record the result; no workflow reads the record and no release step depends on it.

claims.claim: The deployment supports high availability, replication, or multi-region operation.
claims.reason: Out of scope for v1.0. The reference stack is single-node and the limitation is documented.

claims.claim: Release images support multiple CPU architectures.

evidence.name: should publish release images to Docker Hub

claims.claim: The internal CA can be rotated online with a supported command.
claims.reason: CA rotation is not implemented in v1.0. A suspected CA compromise requires a fresh deployment, restore from a pre-compromise backup, new workstation identities, and new agent join tokens.
